stem: A line remains highly heterozygous at many loci. What should a breeder expect when it is used to produce sexually derived offspring?
choices: More opportunity for alleles to segregate into different combinations among offspring
Greater uniformity than a highly homozygous line because heterozygous parents carry more versions of each locus for offspring to share
Reduced recombination across the population because heterozygosity keeps alternative alleles paired together through meiosis
Little inherited variation among offspring because heterozygous loci tend to preserve the parental combination during sexual reproduction
rationale: Heterozygosity means different alleles are present at loci, providing opportunities for segregation and recombination to generate variation among offspring.
